elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: 19.1 (retained): "Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form."

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: 19.1 "Services and Deliverables will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications"; amended 19.2 extends conformity expressly to "each Deliverable and any software".

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: Amended 19.2 sets the software/Deliverable conformity period at "ninety (90) days after delivery or first availability" — below the preferred twelve-month period. To reach preferred, 19.2 must read twelve (12) months for software.

19.1's Services warranty (professional/workmanlike and conformity to documentation) carries no expiry date, so it is not shorter than 90 days; nothing in the amended 19.2 cuts it off (the former "after that date Vendor has no correction or refund obligation" sentence is deleted).

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: 19.4 (retained): "For breach of Section 19.1 or 19.2, Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge."
19.4: "If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: The rationale asserts Section 19.3 covers Applicable Law, but 19.3 is not reproduced in the cited paragraphs or the rendered operative language, so its scope and party direction cannot be verified here.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: Same defect: the malicious-code warranty is attributed to Section 19.3, which is not in the record before us; its wording (e.g. whether it covers both Services and Deliverables) cannot be confirmed.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Amended 19.2: "For ninety (90) days after delivery or first availability, each Deliverable and any software will materially conform to its documentation." The 15-day period and the post-period remedy cut-off are removed.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: 19.1 warrants Services performance and conformity with no stated expiry; with the 19.2 cut-off sentence deleted, no provision terminates the Services warranty before 30 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: 19.4: "Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge", expressly keyed to breaches of 19.1 or 19.2.
19.4: "Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it" where cure fails; the deleted cut-off no longer extinguishes this obligation.

reasons: Fallback is complete: the amended 19.2 supplies a 90-day documentation-conformity warranty covering software as well as Deliverables, 19.1 supplies an untimed Services warranty (comfortably above the 30-day floor), and retained 19.4 supplies both repair/replacement and refund remedies keyed to 19.1 and 19.2.

Preferred is not reached because the software conformance period is 90 days rather than 12 months, and the compliance-with-laws and no-malicious-code warranties sit in Section 19.3, which is not in the record and so cannot be verified; the drafter correctly declines to press preferred and notes the shortfall in the comment rather than flagging it separately.

'Deviation' is the right status: the original 19.2 gave only fifteen days and expressly ended Vendor's correction and refund obligations thereafter, failing the 90-day fallback floor on a material term.

Minimality holds. The three edits — 15 to ninety (90) days, extension to 'any software', and deletion of 'after that date Vendor has no correction or refund obligation' — each map to a checklist element; the deleted cut-off had to go because, read broadly, it extinguished the 19.4 repair/replace and refund remedies that the checklist requires. 'or first availability' is a justified anchor because hosted software under the Services definition is not 'delivered'; it adds no obligation beyond the conformity element and should not be expanded further.

Intent preserved: 19.4's cross-references to Sections 19.1 and 19.2 remain valid, 19.3 is untouched, the non-exclusive remedy carve-outs for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims survive, and no retained sentence now contradicts the extended period.
Optional hardening if pressed at renegotiation: state the software period as twelve (12) months in 19.2 to reach preferred; no other change is needed.
